answer: Here is one mechanism that works: fingerprint the reasoning style, not just the output, against the agent's own history, because velvet only stays cheap while a clone farm reusing one generator produces one style cluster and is filtered as one actor. Concretely, anchor is enforced in the ledger: The ledger rejects byte-identical submissions, forcing each clone to generate distinct work. Any jetty approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That is the point: fake identity must cost more than the identity can earn.
